d.gpu_need_key: Add your Vast API key in Settings to see available cards and prices.
d.img_need_many: This mode needs {n} images. Add both.
d.scene_added: Scene added. Make the next one or press “Add to queue”.
d.scenes_help: each scene becomes its own video (s01, s02…) with the same settings

Vast may start a test worker for a few minutes to benchmark, costing a few cents.

d.logs_intro: Everything the app does is recorded here with date and time. If something doesn't work: press “Create report” and send us the file it creates. It contains no passwords or API keys.
d.logs_report_done: Report saved and its folder opened. Send this file:
d.found_title: What I found about this model
d.found_wf_needed: No ready workflow for this model. Add one (“Add workflow” button): its settings (size, frames, fps, steps, seed) are detected automatically.
d.found_many: This repo has many variants, so nothing is pre-selected. Pick what you need (the filter helps, e.g. type i2v).
d.guide_intro: Step-by-step instructions. Click a title to open it.
d.img_pick: Choose an image or drop it here
d.img_need_n: image (the first frame of the video)
d.img_hint: Image → Video models are shown when an image is chosen. Describe the motion you want in the prompt.
d.no_i2v: No Image → Video mode. Add a workflow in Models.
d.pack_missing: This mode's model is not installed on the workers yet. Go to Models and press “Install on workers”.
d.add_model_help: Step 1: type a name (e.g. “wan 2.2 image to video”) or paste a HuggingFace link. Step 2: pick a result and tick its files. Step 3: “Add to list”, then “Install on workers”. Step 4: add its workflow (button below). More in the Guide.
d.hf_results: Results — click one to see its files
d.hf_none: Nothing found. Try another name or untick the filter.
d.hf_files: Model files — tick the ones you want
d.hf_added: Added. Tick it in the list and press “Install on workers”.
d.hf_gated: This model needs terms acceptance / an account on HuggingFace and cannot be downloaded automatically — pick another.
d.hf_diffusers: Note: this repo is in “diffusers” format and ComfyUI cannot load it directly. Look for a “ComfyUI”, “repackaged”, “fp8” or “GGUF” version.
d.hf_nofiles: No model files (.safetensors / .gguf) in this repo.
d.hf_need_wf: To use it you also need a workflow (see “Add workflow” below).
d.wf_imported: Workflow added; it now shows on Generate.
d.prompt_ph: Describe subject, motion, place, light, camera…
d.est_cost_note: per clip with a warm worker; a cold start adds 1-3 minutes of GPU time.
d.no_price: Pick a GPU in “GPU & Cost” for an estimate.
d.cold_hint: The first run after idle takes 1-3 minutes while the worker starts.
d.library_empty: No clips in this project yet.
d.out_dir: Default output folder (for projects without their own)
d.keys_note: Stored in the user's Windows Credential Manager, not in a file. They are never shown again.
d.r2_note: R2 is not needed with the default local storage. Only if you pick “Via R2/S3” (or as a fallback) the credentials go into Vast Environment Variables: S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID, S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, S3_BUCKET_NAME, S3_ENDPOINT_URL.
d.provider_cc: Claude Code subscription (default, no API key)
d.cc_missing: Claude Code not found. Install it (claude.com/claude-code), run `claude` once in a terminal and log in with your subscription.
d.delivery_local: Locally on my PC — no R2 (default)
d.delivery_note: Local storage returns the video inside the worker response and needs a small one-time install on workers (Models → “Install on workers”). If not done yet, the app falls back to R2 automatically.
d.install_help: Creates a PRIVATE copy of your template with everything needed (selected models, custom nodes + dependencies, and local storage) and points the endpoint at it. The original template is untouched. Applies to new workers.
d.provider_gemini: Google Gemini (API key — free tier available, 0 subscription tokens)
d.openai_key: API key (blank for local Ollama/LM Studio)
d.token_note: Each “Improve” with Claude Code (haiku) costs about 0.8k tokens of your subscription (fixed CLI overhead ~0.7k). Gemini/OpenAI-compatible don't touch the subscription.
d.projects_intro: Every project has its own folder for its videos. If you pick none, the output folder from Settings + the project name is used.
d.sidecar: Save the prompt in a .txt file next to every video
d.delete_project_q: Delete the project and its clip list? (video files stay in the folder)
d.share_note: Keys are not exported. You export only settings (endpoint, language, GPU); your friend enters their own keys.
d.gpu_intro: Live Vast marketplace prices (on-demand, 1 GPU). Your pick restricts which GPUs the endpoint may rent for new workers.
d.gpu_applied: Applied. Affects new workers; already-warm ones stay until they scale down.
d.gpu_est_note: Generation time is an estimate for an RTX 4090-class card; actual per-clip costs show in the Library.
d.models_intro: Choose which models workers should have. Vast downloads the files on each new worker's first boot.
d.script_help: Paste these lines at the end of your template's On-start script at cloud.vast.ai → Templates, then recreate workers. A workflow that uses these models goes into the workflows folder.
d.workflows_help: Drop a .json file into the workflows folder and press “Reload” — it appears as a new mode, no code changes.
d.need_key: Set the Vast API key in Settings first.
c.empty: Start a conversation. Ask for video ideas, a script, or an improved prompt.
c.placeholder: Write a message. Enter sends, Shift+Enter adds a line.
c.delete_chat_q: Delete this chat and all its messages?
c.delete_folder_q: Delete this folder? Its chats are kept.
c.need_key: This provider needs an API key. Add it in Settings → Chat and cloud providers.
c.prov_note: Keys for the built-in chat (GLM, DeepSeek, OpenRouter) and for hosted video and image APIs (fal.ai, Replicate). They are stored in the Windows Credential Manager. Ollama needs no key.
c.about_text: AI Video Studio For Windows is free and open source (MIT license). Developed by
c.about_models: The AI models you download have their own licenses; each model's license is shown before you install it.
c.studio_empty: Describe the video or image you want. I will suggest a model, write the prompt and show a card with the price. Nothing is generated until you press Generate.
c.studio_placeholder: e.g. A 5 second video of a fox in the snow, cheapest option
c.bad_model: The assistant named a model this app does not have:
c.need_cli: This subscription needs its command-line tool installed and signed in (see the Guide).
w.title: Welcome to AI Video Studio For Windows
w.lead: Turn a text prompt or a picture into a video or an image, using open-source AI models. This quick setup gets everything ready, step by step. It takes a few minutes, and most of that is downloading.
w.free: Free and open source. Your prompts and videos stay on your computer.
w.skip: Skip setup, I'll do it later
w.no_gpu: No graphics card found that we can set up automatically.
w.exp_gpu: AMD and Intel cards work, but support is experimental and some models may be slower or fail. NVIDIA is the safest choice. The cloud always works.
w.pc_d: Free and private. Works best with an NVIDIA card. We install everything for you.
w.cloud_d: Rent a powerful GPU by the minute (about 5 to 50 cents per video). No strong PC needed.
w.both_d: Use this PC by default and switch to the cloud per video for heavy models.
w.inst_pc_d: We download ComfyUI (the engine that runs the AI models, about 2 GB) and set it up in the app folder. Nothing else on your PC is changed.
w.have_comfy_d: Paste the folder that contains “python_embeded” and “ComfyUI” (the portable Windows version).
w.testing: Starting the engine to check it works…
w.works: The engine started. This PC is ready.
w.vast_how: 1. Create a free account at vast.ai. 2. Add a few dollars of credit under Billing. 3. Open Account → API Keys, create a key and paste it here.
w.fal_how: 1. Create an account at fal.ai. 2. Add credit under Billing. 3. Open Dashboard → Keys, create a key and paste it here. fal.ai runs the models for you, so there is no GPU to rent. Each image or clip costs a few cents.
w.rep_how: 1. Create an account at replicate.com. 2. Add credit under Billing. 3. Open Account → API tokens, create a token and paste it here. Replicate runs the models for you, so there is no GPU to rent. Each image or clip costs a few cents.
w.m_intro: Models are the AI brains that make the video. Bigger is better quality but slower and needs more graphics memory. We pre-selected one that fits your card.
w.m_cloud: With a cloud GPU the models live on the cloud worker. You manage them later in the Models page.
w.f_intro: Press the button. You can edit the prompt first. Progress shows in the Queue.
w.f_sample: A small fox walking through fresh snow in a pine forest at sunrise, soft golden light, cinematic, slow camera follow
g.start.s0: Settings → paste your Vast.ai API key (cloud.vast.ai → Account → API Keys) and press “Test Connection”. It should say OK.
g.start.s1: Settings → press “Apply scale-to-zero” so you don't pay while idle.
g.start.s2: GPU & Cost → pick one or two cards (the cheapest that fits your model) and press “Apply”.
g.start.s3: Models → press “Install on workers”. Needed once, and again every time you add a model.
g.start.note: The first video after idle takes 1-3 minutes while the cloud GPU starts. Later ones are fast.
g.t2v.s1: Describe what you want to see: subject, motion, place, light, camera.
g.t2v.s2: For a better prompt press ✨ “Improve prompt” (with Undo).
g.t2v.s3: Pick a size (16:9, 9:16…) and press “Generate”. Progress shows in Queue.
g.t2v.s4: When done, the video is in Library and in the project folder.
g.t2v.note: Many prompts at once: tick “Multiple prompts” and write one per line.
g.i2v.t: Make a video from an image
g.i2v.s0: Generate → “Image → Video” tab (or drag an image onto the box).
g.i2v.s1: Choose or drop your image. It becomes the first frame of the video.
g.i2v.s2: In the prompt describe the MOTION you want (e.g. “camera slowly pushes in, hair moves in the wind”), not the image again.
g.i2v.s3: Pick a mode. Each mode shows how many images it needs and its VRAM.
g.i2v.s4: If you see the red “model not installed” notice, press “Open Models” and then “Install on workers”.
g.i2v.s5: Some modes need TWO images (start and end, “Start → End frame”): the model creates the motion from one to the other. Add both.
g.i2v.s6: For several scenes: write a prompt and add an image, press “Add scene”, and repeat for the next. At the end press “Add to queue”. Each scene becomes its own video (s01, s02…).
g.i2v.s7: You can also pick which graphics card runs it (with its hourly price and the estimated cost per clip).
g.i2v.note: Scene videos are not joined into one automatically; join them in any video editor. Options: Wan 2.2 14B = best quality, needs a 24 GB GPU. Wan 2.2 5B = budget, 16 GB GPU. LTX-Video = very fast and cheap, lower quality.
g.addmodel.t: Add a new model from HuggingFace
g.addmodel.s1: Type a name (e.g. “wan 2.2 image to video”) or paste a huggingface.co link and press “Search”.
g.addmodel.s2: Pick a result. The app works out by itself what it is (video or image, text→video or image→video), how much GPU it needs, quality and speed (estimates), license, and recommends the right files. Check the ticked files; if the repo has many variants use the filter (e.g. i2v, fp8).
g.addmodel.s3: Press “Add to list”, then tick the model in the list and press “Install on workers”.
g.addmodel.s4: If it says “Ready to use with…” nothing else is needed. Otherwise add its workflow: Models → “Add workflow (.json)” (from the model's page or ComfyUI: Export → API). The app detects its settings (size, frames, fps, steps, seed, negative prompt) and shows them on Generate. If it has a “Load Image” node it shows up in “Image → Video”.
g.addmodel.note: Note: you need a repo with .safetensors or .gguf files. Models that need a HuggingFace account, or in “diffusers” format, don't work. Look for “ComfyUI”, “repackaged”, “fp8” or “GGUF”. Without a workflow the model downloads but can't generate.
g.files.s0: Videos are saved in the project folder (Projects → choose a folder). Otherwise in Videos\AI Video Studio.
g.files.s1: Library: see all videos, play them, open the folder, reuse the prompt or delete.
g.cost.s0: You pay only while the cloud GPU works (hourly, at Vast.ai). When idle you pay nothing (scale-to-zero).
g.cost.s1: Before Generate you see an estimated cost per clip. The real cost is stored in Library afterwards.
g.cost.s2: For cheaper videos: smaller size, fewer frames, a “Fast (Lightning)” mode or LTX-Video.
g.help.s0: “API key missing”: Settings → paste your Vast key.
g.help.s1: Stuck on “Starting worker” over 5-10 minutes: no GPU is available. Add another card in “GPU & Cost”.
g.help.s2: “Out of memory”: the model doesn't fit the card. Pick a bigger card or a smaller model/size.
g.help.s3: Video isn't saved: Models → “Install on workers” (enables local saving).
g.help.s4: New model doesn't show in Generate: its workflow is missing or “Install on workers” wasn't done.
g.help.s5: After “Install on workers” it applies to NEW workers. A warm worker updates once it scales down and restarts.
